findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without washing their hands in between tasks and cooking. Discussed with PIC. Employees were educated and the behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to always wash their hands before donning gloves during food prep.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following were observed during the inspection.
1. There was no sani bucket available in the kitchen during inspection.
2. Inspector observed an employee using a copy of the menu to wipe off the surface of the prep cooler. 
A staff member was asked to make a sani bucket right away. The sanitizer was tested at 100 ppm. Education was carried out and the prep surface was cleaned and sanitized.  Ensure that all sanitizers are always made at the appropriate concentration and available during food prep at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed mice droppings in multiple places within the facility including a live mouse running across the room in the buffet area. PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that they currently have traps and active pest control treatment going on. Ensure that the frequency of pest control treatment is increase to eliminate pest presence within the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment:
The following were observed. 
1. Two open employee drinks without straws and lids were observed sitting on multiple food contact surfaces.
2. An employee phone was observed stored on the prep surface in the kitchen. 
PIC was made aware. The items mentioned were removed and stored appropriately. Ensure that employees use the designated storage areas for their personal items including using containers with a lid and straw for drinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The standing cooler in the kitchen was observed not holding the appropriate temperature range.  PIC was made aware. PIC informed inspector that the food items in the cooler were placed in the cooler on 6/14/2026 (two days prior to the inspection). The food items in the cooler was discarded. The cooler was repaired and the ambient temperature collected was 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There was no hanging thermometer present in the standing cooler in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC provided a hanging thermometer for the cooler. Ensure that there is always a hanging thermometer present in all cold holding units at all times.

(A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: A pan filled with chicken breast was observed being thawed sitting a water in the triple sink. Education on appropriated thawing methods as stated within the 2022 FDA food code was carried out. The chicken breast was later placed under running water to be properly thawed. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable about the appropriate thawing methods to avoid food contamination and spoilage.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple cardboard boxes with food items being stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler by the dry storage. PIC was made aware of the cardboard boxes with food items being stored on the floor. PIC said that they would have them remove from the floor. Ensure that containers and boxes with food items are stored at least 6” above the floor.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:

2. A knife was observed lodged in the space between the prep counter space on the large prep cooler and a cardboard box of single use food storage sheets in the kitchen. 
Education was carried out. The knives were removed and taken to be cleaned. Ensure that in-use or between-use utensils are stored properly.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION. Inspectors observed facility not being in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the person with the CFPM certification will get the training done as soon as possible. Ensure that at least one certified food protection manager at the facility obtain a basic allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following violations in storage order:
1. Raw sausages were stored above cheese in the bottom of the prep cooler.
2. Raw eggs were observed being stored above cooked pulled pork in the bottom of the prep cooler. 
Discussed with PIC and the corrections were made. Ensure that the appropriate storage order for food items is observed to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed facility not being in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the person with the CFPM certification will get the training done as soon as possible. Ensure that at least one certified food protection manager at the facility obtain a basic allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
